name: needs-proactive-queue-visual
description: Visual check of proactive need queuing: dispatch an employee to work so no rest can be claimed, drive fatigue below its warning threshold (25), then verify the auto-inserted rest task appears both in the pending-actions state dump and as a queued task in the roster panel

steps.description: Opens the Crew panel with ensurePanel rather than a bare toolbar click (#556): the toolbar tab toggles, so when a preceding step has already opened the panel a second click closes it and the hire button underneath reports zero size.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- employees.ts's own `dispatch` case comment: "no console command currently creates one... which left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design, same class as `employee assign_skill`.

expect.note: the dispatched work task itself, queued and not yet claimed

Re-measured for #928 (single-gauge/fatigue model): the dispatch completes within this batch (as #547 already fixed), and fatigue only drops to ~44.45 over these 40 ticks -- comfortably above the 25 warning threshold, so no rest is queued yet. pendingActionCount is 0, not 1.

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

Placed away from the (10,10) dispatch target (#437) — building on top of the employee's own tile made that cell permanently NavGrid-blocked with the employee still standing on it, so every later rest/collapse routing failed to path out and the employee got stuck COLLAPSING at 0/0/0 needs forever instead of demonstrating the queued-rest recovery this scenario is about.

expect.note: Re-measured for #928: the driller's dispatched work already completed by tick 40 (previous step), so only the freshly-queued construction site itself counts here -- pendingActionCount reads 1, not 2.

#945 (fatigue rest under-restoration + mid-task/mid-drive rest preemption): net direction corrected decreased -> increased for minFatigue. Over this 80-tick window (construction work, tick 40 -> 120) fatigue still dips below the warning threshold mid-batch and triggers a proactive/collapse-adjacent rest that is claimed, walked to, and completed, but that rest no longer under-restores -- it now brings fatigue up to a genuine recovery level (measured 71.00 at this checkpoint) before the natural working decline through tick 120 resumes, landing net ABOVE its tick-40 value (~44.45) instead of below it. This is the fix's own intended behaviour, not a regression: rest that leaves an employee barely better off than before it started was the #945 bug. pendingActionCount is 0 at both endpoints (nothing left queued or mid-claim by tick 120).
